lots.what_it_is: Leather rifle bucket (303 / SMLE pattern) with brass buckles and sling strap, strap stamped M HARVEY & CO LTD / WALSALL / 1940. Gowans title says Light Horse and 1920; my reading of the stamp is 1940, so WWII era, not WWI.
lots.guide_summary: No surviving evidence of any kind. The researcher found nothing (WebSearch budget exhausted) and my own WebSearch was also refused (budget 200 of 200 used). Direct tries at Militaria Shop, eMedals, Lawsons, Invaluable and Saleroom searches gave no rifle bucket results with prices. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid. Gowans premium 19.8% noted. A real search of militaria dealers and Australian auction archives (rifle bucket, Walsall 1940, Light Horse) is needed before bidding.
lots.confidence_reason: Maker and date read from the photo, but no comparable prices at all.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 strap stamp reads M HARVEY & CO LTD / WALSALL / 1940; the third digit looks like a 4, not a 2, though the impression is worn. A stitched M or W style mark sits on the adjacent keeper. No broad arrow or unit mark seen in the two photos. Leather mottled and darkened, stitching mostly intact, brass buckles with verdigris, sling strap present, top retaining strap and stud intact.
lots.condition: Used, patinated leather with surface staining and wear; no visible tears or missing stitching in the photos; brass fittings original with some verdigris.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm the strap date (it reads 1940 to us, not 1920) and whether there are any other stamps such as a broad arrow, D^D or unit marks, and any basis for the Light Horse attribution. Any cracks, splits or dry rot in the leather, and is the inner lining sound?

lots.what_it_is: Olympus OM system kit: black Olympus OM body in half case (model name not visible; OM-1 instruction book included, so probably OM-1 black but not confirmed) with lens fitted under an Olympus cap, ever-ready case, boxed OM focusing screens (1-13, 1-1 and one other), boxed OM eyecup, coloured filters, flash bracket, a Fuji pouch, a boxed large framed Fresnel-type lens accessory, and a separate Olympus zoom lens with a PASSED sticker that looks like a digital-era Zuiko (Four Thirds / Micro Four Thirds), not an OM-mount lens.

asking.venue: The Camera Exchange, Box Hill South VIC (dealer)
asking.note: Page opened (curl, JSON-LD: Olympus OM-1 w/ 50mm f1.8, excellent condition in full working order, all caps, AUD 395, InStock). Dealer retail asking price, not a price paid. Tested body plus 50mm lens only, so it is a ceiling for body and lens; our body model and lens are not confirmed and it is untested. No conversion.

lots.guide_summary: One asking price only: A$395 dealer retail for a tested OM-1 with 50mm f1.8. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 1 asking. No exchange rate used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid. A dealer asking price for a tested camera overstates what an untested room-auction kit realises.
lots.confidence_reason: Body model unread (only the OM-1 book points to it), fitted lens unidentified, rests on one asking price.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. The researcher's single Camera Exchange entry checked out (price, description and stock status match). Researcher's identification adjusted: body model is not confirmed as OM-1, and the loose zoom appears to be a digital-era Zuiko lens rather than an OM lens.
lots.key_photo_findings: Black body with OLYMPUS on the prism and an R marking near the front lower left; model name hidden. Lens on the body capped with an Olympus 49mm-style cap, so focal length unknown. Boxes read OM System Focusing Screen 1-13, Focusing Screen 1-1, another Focusing Screen box, and OM Eyecup 1. OM-1 instruction book. Loose zoom lens has silver ring and red dot styling typical of digital Zuiko lenses with a PASSED QC sticker. Large boxed item top left is a black-framed acrylic Fresnel/condenser-style lens, purpose not identified.
lots.condition: Cosmetically tidy in the single photo; working order unknown (OM-1 meters often need conversion for the old mercury cell, and shutters and light seals may need service).
lots.question_for_gowans: What model is the body (OM-1, OM-1n, OM-2?) and which lens is fitted (focal length and aperture)? Does the shutter fire and does the meter respond? What mount is the loose zoom lens with the PASSED sticker, and what is the large boxed framed lens accessory?
